metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward recent 7-day average if sentiment shifts >1.5 units.
- For 30-day forecasts, model overestimates when sentiment is mixed or trending upward; apply downward bias of 3–8% if sentiment >50% positive.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after high forecast, model often lags; add 1–3 day lag correction for 15–30 day horizons when sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is uniformly negative and price drops >5% from prior day, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
